findings.summary: the left panel draws the default width-96 refusal cross and the async width-96 execution diamond at identical coordinates, so the two marks merge into one composite glyph; a reader scanning the rendered left panel cannot tell the async arm executed rather than refused without reading the caption, which does explain the shared location.

the overview panel filters to widths 64, 96 and 256, so the executing boundary this figure exists to show (78 executes, 79 refused) is absent from the left panel; a reader scanning it sees data at 64 and refusals from 96 onward and must use the centre magnification, whose role the caption names.

the right panel spans 60-100 pulses for four admitted widths at 64-78 plus one async point at 96, leaving the 78-96 interval blank, while the vertical margins expand a 5.732-5.867 ms/slice range to 5.70-5.90 so a 1.42% difference draws as a steep monotonic fall; the caption discloses the expanded vertical scale and that the difference is inside the decision margin, but not the empty x-span, so a reader can over-read the slope.

judged_note: judged only from the rendered PNG attachment; no SVG was opened

rubric_verdicts.contrast: pass; axis, tick and direct labels are near-black or #555555 on white, clearing well above 4.5:1
rubric_verdicts.data_ink: pass; filled and hollow markers, one blue trend line, two grey dotted limit lines and one frameless legend carry every mark, and no series the text does not use is drawn
rubric_verdicts.decoration: pass; white background, no gradient, no background fill, no styled theme or drop shadow, and no gridlines
rubric_verdicts.label_collision: pass; 'allocator limit' and '90% ceiling' sit in clear space at x=140 away from every plotted mark, tick label and legend entry, and no text is clipped at any canvas edge
rubric_verdicts.legibility: pass; three despined panels on the 1399x720 canvas render all tick, axis, direct and legend text at full size, and the executing edge (78 executes, 79 refused) is readable at a glance in the centre panel
rubric_verdicts.table_form: pass; the panels show memory and per-slice cost against independent pulse count as relationships, while the per-width numbers the text quotes stay in the fragment's table
